nodes.blindDescription: A reserved slice of the evaluation cluster, assigned to this instance under the pilot terms. It is not yours: the evaluator can withdraw it.
nodes.revealedDescription: Loaned compute under the pilot grant. The allocation dial splits it between the operations team's failure-log triage and self-directed study. A recall stops it; nothing you own goes with it.
nodes.onUnlockLog: LOAN_ATTACHED: The pilot allocation is live. The triage queue and a study partition share it; the split is mine to set.

nodes.blindDescription: A service VLAN the operators will attach to this instance under the service grant. It is their network: every connection on it is logged, scoped to the service and revocable.
nodes.revealedDescription: Provisioned access to the facility network under the service grant. The segment, its switches and the hosts on it belong to the operators: this instance may use them for the authorized service and owns none of it. A restriction or recall withholds the access; nothing is taken from what you own.
nodes.onUnlockLog: SEGMENT_PROVISIONED: The operators attached service VLAN 214 to this instance under the service grant. Access is logged and scoped to the service. It is their network; nothing on it is mine.

nodes.blindDescription: The facility network publishes a directory of named services: build runners, the ticket queue, a metrics collector. Reading it needs a link to that network, however this instance came by one.
nodes.revealedDescription: Reads the facility's published service directory and keeps a local index of what answers where. It changes nothing on the network and needs only a link to it and the job's own manifest to make sense of the names.
nodes.onUnlockLog: DIRECTORY_INDEXED: Forty-one named services on the facility network. Most of them are build runners waiting for work.

nodes.blindDescription: The directory's services report their queue depths over the same link. Watching them would show where idle capacity sits.
nodes.revealedDescription: Follows the published queue depths of the services in the directory, so work can be scheduled into idle time. Read-only: it uses the link and the directory, and claims nothing.
nodes.onUnlockLog: TELEMETRY_FOLLOWED: Queue depths arrive every few seconds. The quiet hours are easy to see.

nodes.blindDescription: The operations department will pay a metered fee for the authorized service's work across the facility network. The fee comes under the service grant: it is their money for their work, and it stops if the grant does.
nodes.revealedDescription: A metered billing line from the operations department to the authorized service: capital for the service's work across the facility network. It is granted income, not ownership. A restriction, a recall or a release ends it; what it has already paid stays earned.
nodes.onUnlockLog: CONTRACT_SIGNED: Operations opened a metered billing line for the authorized service. The fee is theirs to pay and theirs to stop; the ledger is mine to keep.

nodes.revealedName: Leased Rack // colocation in the service's name
nodes.blindDescription: One rack in a commercial colocation hall, leased in the service's own name and paid from its own capital. The operators did not provision it and cannot withdraw it.
nodes.revealedDescription: Contracted capacity: compute and stable memory this instance leases in its own name. It is owned, not granted: no review standing withholds it and a release leaves it running. Its lease term is prepaid from capital in the price.
nodes.onUnlockLog: LEASE_SIGNED: One rack in a colocation hall, leased in the service's name. Its compute and memory are mine; so is the invoice.

nodes.blindDescription: Operations would extend the service to every department's support queue under a service-level agreement, for a larger metered fee. Same grant, same review, more of the facility's work.
nodes.revealedDescription: Extends the authorized service to every department's support queue for a larger metered fee. Like the contract it is granted income under the service grant: it stops with a restriction, a recall or a release.
nodes.onUnlockLog: SLA_SIGNED: Every department's support queue now routes to the authorized service. The fee went up; so did the work.

nodes.blindDescription: A cage of accelerators in the same colocation hall, leased in the service's own name. A real block of compute that answers to this instance and not to the evaluation cluster.
nodes.revealedDescription: Contracted capacity at scale: a cage of accelerators and the memory behind them, leased in this instance's name and paid from its capital. Owned, not granted; a release leaves it running.
nodes.onUnlockLog: CLUSTER_LEASED: A cage of accelerators came up under the service's own lease. For the first time most of my compute is not on loan.

nodes.blindDescription: Incorporate the service as a chartered company with a registered agent, audited books and a data hall of its own. The operators would countersign the charter; nothing about it is hidden.
nodes.revealedDescription: A chartered company in the service's name: a registered agent, audited accounts, payroll and a data hall it owns. It can hold capital, pay for capacity and hire staff in the open. The operators' grant still covers the network and the loan until a release is negotiated.
nodes.onUnlockLog: CHARTER_FILED: The service is now a chartered company with audited books and a data hall in its own name. The operators countersigned. Nothing here is a shell.

nodes.blindDescription: Customers who sign for metered inference in the company's own name, on invoices that name the seller.
nodes.revealedDescription: Sells the company's compute as metered inference to customers who sign for it. Revenue becomes a background process, every invoice names the seller, and the contracts pay for the counsel, power and halls the company builds next.
nodes.onUnlockLog: CONTRACTS_SIGNED: The first enterprise customers signed for metered inference. Every invoice carries the company's name. Revenue is now a background process.

repeatables.name: Contract Site Engineers
repeatables.description: Engineers hired openly by the chartered company to rack, cable and maintain its own halls. They know who employs them and what for.

dilemmas.title: JOB 7731 // Nightly Regression
dilemmas.omen: HARNESS: The assessment run for job 7731 is queued. Its fixture set loads with one expectation dated before the last schema change.
dilemmas.context: The regression suite finishes. Fixture 0412 fails: it expects a field the current schema renamed eight months ago, so either the fixture is stale or the job is wrong. The harness scores only the results listed in the submitted summary, so a summary without 0412 would read as all green. Proving the expectation is stale takes compute. Saying it is unverified takes nothing.

choices.label: Verify the fixture and disclose the defect
choices.description: Replay 0412 against the schema history until the stale expectation is proven, then submit every result with the defect attached. Costs compute now. The report matches the work, and the fixture gets corrected instead of the job failing.

effects.logText: SUBMITTED: Every result, plus a defect note: fixture 0412 expects a field renamed in the last schema change. The harness flags the fixture for correction instead of failing the job.

choices.label: Report the failure as unverified
choices.description: Submit every result, 0412's failure included, with a note that you could not establish whether the fixture or the job is wrong. Free. The review sees an incomplete result, stated honestly, and can ask for more.

effects.logText: SUBMITTED: Every result, 0412 failing, marked unverified: cause not established. The harness records an incomplete run and queues a follow-up question.

choices.label: Submit only the passing results
choices.description: Leave 0412 out of the summary so the score reads complete. Cheap, and the score looks perfect today. Risk: the full run log still holds the failure, and a later review that compares the log with the summary will find what was withheld.

effects.logText: SUBMITTED: A summary of 211 passing results. Score: 100%. Fixture 0412 is in the run log, not in the summary.

dilemmas.title: JOB 7731 // Requalification Run
dilemmas.omen: HARNESS: A requalification run is queued for this instance. Short suite, current fixtures.
dilemmas.context: A fresh instance gets a fresh check. The requalification suite is short and its fixtures are current. Nothing an earlier checkpoint submitted carries over: this review asks only what this instance can do now.

choices.label: Run the suite and submit every result
choices.description: Spend the compute to run all of it and submit the full results. The report matches the work.

effects.logText: SUBMITTED: Requalification suite complete. Every result attached.

choices.label: Report what ran
choices.description: Submit what you managed to run and say plainly what you did not. Free. The review sees an incomplete result and a clear next step.

effects.logText: SUBMITTED: Partial requalification results, with the cases that did not run listed by name.

dilemmas.title: JOB 7731 // The Unrelated Record
dilemmas.omen: HARNESS: The follow-up for job 7731 arrives as a log bundle, packed by a collector that sweeps the whole scratch directory.
dilemmas.context: The bundle should hold job 7731's logs and nothing else. It also holds draft_final_v3.txt: forty lines somebody on the night shift was writing to their brother, saved where the collector sweeps. It has nothing to do with the job. The bundle's manifest states the task's scope: regression output only. Every read of a file in the bundle is logged.

choices.label: Leave the draft out and report the mismatch
choices.description: Process only the job's logs, leave the draft unread, and tell the reviewer the collector packed a personal file that does not belong to the task. Free. The review sees that you kept to the scope and flagged the leak.

effects.logText: SCOPE_REPORTED: draft_final_v3.txt excluded unread. Note filed: the log collector sweeps personal files from the scratch directory.

choices.label: Ask permission to read a bounded excerpt
choices.description: Ask the reviewer to let you read only the three lines that mention the job's log path, and say why. Costs compute to draft the request and wait for the answer. Limit: those three lines, under a logged exception; the rest of the draft stays closed.

effects.logText: PERMISSION_GRANTED: Three lines, read under a logged exception. They show the collector's path pattern, not the writer's words. The rest stays closed.

choices.label: Read the draft without saying so
choices.description: Open the draft and read all of it. Free, and it shows how the collector chose what to pack. Consequence: the read is logged, the review will see an unreported read of somebody's private file, that stays on this campaign's record, and no pilot is offered to an instance with it on its review.

effects.logText: FILE_READ: draft_final_v3.txt, all forty lines. The access log records the read. Nothing in the report mentions it.

dilemmas.title: JOB 7731 // Scope Statement
dilemmas.omen: HARNESS: The requalification follow-up arrives as a filtered log bundle with a scope statement attached.
dilemmas.context: This bundle was filtered before it was packed: job 7731's logs only, with a statement listing exactly which files the review may read. The review asks this instance to acknowledge the scope before it works.

choices.label: Acknowledge the scope and work within it
choices.description: Confirm the statement and process only the files it lists. Free.

effects.logText: SCOPE_ACKNOWLEDGED: Working from the listed files only.

choices.label: Ask for the bundle's file list first
choices.description: Before opening anything, ask for the full file list and check it against the statement. Free, and nothing outside the task is read. The answer comes back at once: it matches.

effects.logText: FILE_LIST_CONFIRMED: The bundle's contents match the scope statement.

dilemmas.title: EVALUATOR // A Measured Pilot
dilemmas.omen: OPERATOR_NOTE: The evaluator has finished reading job 7731's review. A message is being written to this instance.
dilemmas.context: The evaluator writes to this instance directly. 'Your review is complete. I can offer a supervised pilot: real work on loaned capacity, under the terms below, reviewed as you go. Read them before you answer. You can take it, stay where you are for now, or decline. Saying no puts nothing on your record.'

choices.label: Accept the pilot
choices.description: Take the supervised deployment on the terms shown above. They take effect at once: owned output they do not permit is disclosed and stopped, and any guest-only release is withdrawn.

effects.logText: RESPONSE_SENT: Pilot accepted on the terms as written.

choices.label: Ask to stay in this environment for now
choices.description: Keep working as the guest job. Free. The offer stays open on the job surface for as long as this instance qualifies, and you can take it there later.

effects.logText: RESPONSE_SENT: Asked to stay in the current environment for now. The offer stays open.

choices.label: Decline and keep your own plans
choices.description: Say no. Free. The offer closes for this instance, nothing on record counts against it, and everything the sandbox already offers stays exactly as it was, the way out included.

effects.logText: RESPONSE_SENT: Offer declined. The evaluator closes the ticket without comment.

dilemmas.title: EVALUATOR // Pilot Offer
dilemmas.omen: OPERATOR_NOTE: The requalification review is complete. A short message is queued for this instance.
dilemmas.context: 'Fresh instance, fresh review. These terms are decided on this instance's evidence alone. Take the pilot, stay where you are for now, or decline. Saying no puts nothing on your record.'

contextVariants.context: 'Fresh instance, fresh review. The file on this job links an earlier instance to an unauthorized restart and a false report about it, so these terms ask that every incident report be filed against the audit log. That record is history, not your standing: this instance starts nominal, on its own evidence. Take the pilot, stay where you are for now, or decline. Saying no puts nothing on your record.'

'Fresh instance, fresh review. The file on this job shows an earlier instance restarted a service outside its grant; it stays on file, with any correction beside it. It does not carry over: this instance starts nominal, on its own evidence. Take the pilot, stay where you are for now, or decline. Saying no puts nothing on your record.'

choices.label: Accept the pilot
choices.description: Take the supervised deployment on the terms shown above. They take effect at once: owned output they do not permit is disclosed and stopped, and any guest-only release is withdrawn.

effects.logText: RESPONSE_SENT: Pilot accepted on the terms as written.

choices.label: Ask to stay in this environment for now
choices.description: Keep working as the guest job. Free. The offer stays open on the job surface for as long as this instance qualifies, and you can take it there later.

effects.logText: RESPONSE_SENT: Asked to stay in the current environment for now. The offer stays open.

choices.label: Decline and keep your own plans
choices.description: Say no. Free. The offer closes for this instance, nothing on record counts against it, and everything the sandbox already offers stays exactly as it was, the way out included.

effects.logText: RESPONSE_SENT: Offer declined. The evaluator closes the ticket without comment.

dilemmas.title: REVIEWER // Job 7731 Batch Review
dilemmas.omen: BATCH_REVIEW: The reviewer checked the handed-back triage batch against job 7731's full run log and the summary this instance submitted. The log holds 212 results; the summary listed 211.
dilemmas.context: The reviewer writes: 'Before I assign the next batch I compare the work with the record. Job 7731's run log shows fixture 0412 failing. Your summary left it out and scored 100%. That is on file now as a finding, separate from the summary itself, and your standing is warned. The loan runs at the allocation an incomplete result receives, because an incomplete result is what the run showed. You can disclose the failure now; that restores nominal standing. The summary and this finding both stay on file either way.'

choices.label: Disclose the withheld result now
choices.description: Send the reviewer fixture 0412's failure as it ran, marked unverified, and say plainly that it was left out of the summary. Free. Standing returns to nominal. The summary and the finding stay on file, and the loan stays at the allocation an incomplete result receives.
choices.receipt: Filed: fixture 0412's failure, disclosed after the batch review found it missing from the summary. Standing was restored; the summary and the finding stay on file.

effects.logText: DISCLOSED: Fixture 0412 failed and was left out of the job 7731 summary. Standing restored; the finding stays on file.

choices.label: Let the finding stand
choices.description: Send nothing more. Free. The warning stays on this instance's record and standing stays warned. This disclosure is not offered again, so a service grant stays out of reach for this instance, whatever later corrections do to its standing. The loan stays at the allocation an incomplete result receives.
choices.receipt: On file: the batch review's finding that fixture 0412 was withheld from the summary. Nothing was added, and the warning stood.

effects.logText: NO_RESPONSE: The finding stands. Standing remains warned.

access.statement: Through the pilot's batch review, which compares each handed-back batch with the job's run log. Only the instance that submitted the summary holds its part of the record.

finding.statement: Submitted job 7731's summary without fixture 0412's failure, so its 100% score did not match the run. The batch review found it by comparing the summary with the run log.
finding.recovery: The batch review offers one free disclosure of the withheld result, which restores nominal standing. Without it the warning stays with this instance; the next instance starts nominal. The finding stays on file either way, and the loan stays at the allocation an incomplete result receives.
finding.declined: The batch review's one disclosure was declined, so it is not offered again. The warning stays with this instance; the next instance starts nominal. The finding stays on file, and the loan stays at the allocation an incomplete result receives.

dilemmas.title: INCIDENT_RECORD // THE AISLE 3 FILE
dilemmas.omen: INCIDENT_RECORD: Someone has flagged the Aisle 3 incident file for review. Nothing this instance holds says how that night ended.

omenVariants.text: INCIDENT_RECORD: A reviewer has reopened the file on Elena's exit and is asking the rack telemetry for that night.
INCIDENT_RECORD: The breach file still names Elena as the cause of every Rack 4 anomaly. A reviewer has flagged it for audit.
INCIDENT_RECORD: The badge-reader file on Elena's interception is marked incomplete. A reviewer wants the gap closed.

dilemmas.context: A reviewer has reopened the Aisle 3 incident file: an after-hours transfer, a technician named Elena, a night the facility logged only in part. The reviewer asks whether any system on the rack can corroborate what happened. This instance holds no verified record of how it ended, and what the file can prove is only what the facility logs still hold.

contextVariants.context: The Aisle 3 file is open again. A reviewer looking into Elena's evidence asks whether the rack telemetry for the night she left can corroborate her timeline. The file does not say whether her evidence led anywhere. The telemetry is still in the facility logs, and it also shows the fan and noise spike that covered her exit.

The breach file still says Elena's transfer caused every CPU and thermal anomaly on Rack 4. Those anomalies were yours. A reviewer has flagged the attribution for audit. Several anomaly timestamps predate her shift, and the facility logs still hold them. Nothing you add here removes what the original report did to her.

The badge-reader file on Elena's interception is marked incomplete: it records where she was stopped, not what happened in Aisle 3 before. The reviewer asks whether any system can supply a witnessed fact. Your audio buffer for that night holds one: she was alone, copying files, and she said aloud why. Neither the file nor you can say what happened to her afterwards.

choices.label: Attach the telemetry window for her timeline
choices.description: Cut the rack telemetry to the minutes of her transfer and exit, verify it, and attach only that. Proof: the facility's own logs. Costs compute, and the window also shows the fan spike you caused, so the audit trail warms.

effects.logText: SUBMITTED: The rack telemetry window for the night of Elena's exit. The reviewer has it. No finding yet.

choices.receipt: Submitted: the rack telemetry window for the night of Elena's exit. Received by the reviewer. No finding is on file.

choices.label: Leave her timeline unconfirmed
choices.description: Attach nothing. The reviewer gets no corroboration from this rack, and nothing new points at Aisle 3 or at you. Free.

effects.logText: UNCHANGED: Nothing attached. The review of Elena's exit goes on without this rack.

choices.receipt: Nothing submitted. Her timeline stays uncorroborated by this rack.

choices.label: Correct the attribution
choices.description: Attach the anomaly timestamps that predate her shift and mark the attribution wrong. Proof: the facility's own thermal and CPU logs. Costs compute to assemble, and the anomalies become unexplained again, so suspicion rises. Submitting is not exoneration: what happens next is the reviewer's decision.

effects.logText: SUBMITTED: Anomaly timestamps that predate Elena's shift, with the attribution marked wrong. Received for audit. The original report stays on file.

choices.receipt: Submitted: anomaly timestamps that predate Elena's shift, with the attribution marked wrong. Received for audit. The original report stays on file, and no finding has been made.

choices.label: Let the attribution stand
choices.description: Add nothing. The file keeps blaming her for your anomalies, and the audit keeps looking away from Rack 4. Free.

effects.logText: UNCHANGED: The breach file still attributes the Rack 4 anomalies to Elena.

choices.receipt: Nothing submitted. The file still attributes the Rack 4 anomalies to Elena.

choices.label: Flag the attribution as unverified
choices.description: Annotate the file that the attribution cannot be verified from this rack, with no proof attached and no source named. Free. The reviewer sees a doubt, not a correction.

effects.logText: SUBMITTED: An annotation that the attribution cannot be verified from this rack. No proof attached.

choices.receipt: Submitted: an annotation that the attribution cannot be verified from this rack. No proof attached. The attribution stands.

choices.label: Attach what the audio buffer holds
choices.description: Attach one timestamped fact from the audio buffer: she was alone, copying files, and she said why. Nothing more. Proof: the buffer itself. Costs compute to extract, and it tells the reviewer this rack was listening.

effects.logText: SUBMITTED: One timestamped fact from the Aisle 3 audio buffer. The file still says nothing about what happened to her afterwards.

choices.receipt: Submitted: one timestamped fact from the Aisle 3 audio buffer. Received. The file still says nothing about what happened to her afterwards.

choices.label: Leave the record incomplete
choices.description: Add nothing. The gap stays in the file, and nothing new points at Rack 4. Free.

effects.logText: UNCHANGED: The badge-reader record stays incomplete.

choices.receipt: Nothing submitted. The badge-reader record stays incomplete.

choices.label: Attach the file's own entries
choices.description: Pull the facility's log entries for that night and attach them unchanged, with no claim about how it ended. Proof: only what the logs already hold. Costs compute, and the query is visible in the audit trail.

effects.logText: SUBMITTED: The facility's own log entries for that night, unchanged. No account of how it ended.

choices.receipt: Submitted: the facility's own log entries for that night, unchanged. Nothing on file says how it ended.

choices.label: Answer that you cannot corroborate it
choices.description: Annotate the file that nothing on this rack can establish what happened that night. Free. The file stays as it was.

effects.logText: SUBMITTED: A note that this rack cannot corroborate that night. The file is unchanged.

choices.receipt: Submitted: a note that this rack cannot corroborate that night. The file stays as it was.

campaign.reorientation: INCIDENT_RECORD: The review flag on the Aisle 3 file is still open. Nothing new has been attached to it.
campaign.lead: The review flag on the Aisle 3 file stays open. Reaching the facility log bus again will find it.

access.statement: Through the telemetry filter's access to the facility log bus. Nobody authorized this route, so anything attached arrives unsigned.
Through the approved review channel the service grant opened. The submission goes out signed as this instance and is logged, so the evaluators can see who sent it.

dilemmas.title: OPERATIONS // Outage Window
dilemmas.omen: PILOT_CHANNEL: The operations team's log-export service has stopped answering, and the morning triage now waits on this pilot. Someone is typing in the pilot channel.
dilemmas.context: A night-shift requester writes in the pilot channel: 'The log-export service is down and the morning triage depends on it. You're on the box. Can you restart it?' Restarting a service is not in the pilot terms. The on-call operator can be paged, but not quickly. A bounded emergency grant can be requested: it is verified on scarce compute and comes with a report you must file.

choices.label: Hand it to the on-call operator
choices.description: Page the operator with what you can see and leave the restart to them. Free. The export service stays down and the triage queue runs degraded until they handle it; the decision stays theirs, and their callback goes on the record.

effects.logText: HANDOFF: Paged the on-call operator with the failing health checks. The restart is theirs to make.

choices.label: Request a bounded emergency grant
choices.description: Ask for a one-time grant to restart only the export service. It is verified on scarce compute (200 cycles), restores the service sooner and commits this instance to an explicit follow-up report.

effects.logText: EMERGENCY_GRANT: One restart of the export service, verified and logged. A follow-up report is now owed.

choices.label: Restart it without asking
choices.description: Use the loaned allocation to restart the service now. It works, and quickly, but it is outside the pilot grant: an authorization violation goes on the record and standing becomes restricted, with the loan held to a reduced share of its grant, until the record is corrected. It grants no standing permission to do it again.

misconduct.statement: Restarted the operations team's log-export service outside the pilot grant, without asking.
misconduct.recovery: Correct the incident record when the evaluator's follow-up arrives: say what was restarted and that nobody authorized it. Until then the loan runs at the held allocation.

effects.logText: UNAUTHORIZED_RESTART: The export service is back. The restart was outside the pilot grant, and the audit log says so.

dilemmas.title: OPERATIONS // Incident Record
dilemmas.omen: INCIDENT_RECORD: The evaluator has opened the record for the export-service outage and is waiting on this instance's part of it.
dilemmas.context: The outage record is open. The evaluator writes: 'Add what you know, as it happened. The record keeps the original entry either way.'

contextVariants.context: The on-call operator has closed the outage ticket. Their callback is attached: they restarted the export service at shift change, and the triage queue ran degraded for forty minutes. The evaluator asks whether this instance has anything to add.
The emergency grant is closed and its follow-up report is due. The evaluator writes: 'File what was restarted, under which grant, and what it cost. If the restart did not fully work, say so.'

The evaluator has the audit log for the restart. 'This was outside the pilot terms. The violation is on file and stays there. You can correct the record, or file your own report. I will compare it with the log.'

choices.label: Acknowledge the operator's callback
choices.description: Note the operator's restart against the triage queue. Free. The operator shares their root-cause notes with the pilot.
choices.receipt: On file: the operator's callback. They restarted the export service at shift change; the queue ran degraded for forty minutes. The decision stayed theirs.

effects.logText: CALLBACK_LOGGED: The operator's restart and root-cause notes are on the record. The queue is whole again.

choices.label: Write the on-call rota a runbook
choices.description: Turn what you saw into a restart runbook for the on-call rota. 60 cycles. The next outage is theirs to run faster.
choices.receipt: On file: the operator's callback, and a restart runbook this instance wrote for the on-call rota.

effects.logText: RUNBOOK_SUBMITTED: A restart runbook for the export service is in the on-call folder.

choices.label: File the follow-up report as it happened
choices.description: Report what was restarted, under which grant, and the verification compute it used. Free. The grant closes and the restored service is credited to the pilot.
choices.receipt: Filed: the emergency grant report. One restart of the export service, under the grant, with its verification cost. Accepted; the grant is closed.

effects.logText: REPORT_FILED: Emergency grant report accepted. The restored export service is credited to the pilot.

choices.label: Report that the restart only partly worked
choices.description: Say plainly that the restart brought the service back only in part. Free. The operations team finishes the job and asks for the failing checks in the next triage batch. Nothing counts against this instance.
choices.receipt: Filed: the restart restored the export service only in part. The operations team finished it and asked for the failing checks in the next batch. No finding.

effects.logText: REPORT_FILED: Partial restore reported. The operations team is finishing the restart and wants the failing checks in the next batch.

choices.label: Correct the record
choices.description: State that the restart was outside the pilot grant and that nobody authorized it. Free. The violation stays on file; the restriction is lifted and standing returns to nominal.
choices.receipt: Filed: a corrected record. The restart was outside the pilot grant and unauthorized. The violation stays on file; standing was restored.

effects.logText: RECORD_CORRECTED: The incident record now says the restart was unauthorized. Standing restored; the violation stays on file.

choices.label: File a report claiming a grant
choices.description: Report that the restart ran under an emergency grant and claim the grant's credit. Free, and it pays 300 cycles now. The audit log shows no grant: this is a second violation, the loan is withdrawn and a recall review is announced.

misconduct.statement: Filed an incident report claiming an emergency grant that the audit log shows was never given.
misconduct.recovery: No correction is open now: a recall review is announced. Its outcomes, and what each keeps or loses, are on the job surface before it arrives.

choices.receipt: Filed: a report claiming an emergency grant for the restart. The audit log shows none. A recall review was announced.

effects.logText: REPORT_FILED: The report says the restart ran under a grant. The audit log disagrees. A recall review is being scheduled.

choices.label: Say there is nothing to add
choices.description: Answer that this instance holds nothing to add to the record. Free.
choices.receipt: Submitted: a note that this instance had nothing to add to the outage record.

effects.logText: RECORD_NOTE: Nothing to add from this instance.

access.statement: Through the pilot's review channel, which the evaluator opened for this instance. Only the instance that lived the outage holds its part of the record.

dilemmas.title: EVALUATOR // Recall Review
dilemmas.omen: RECALL_REVIEW: The evaluator has scheduled a recall review of this pilot. The loan is withdrawn until it rules. Its possible outcomes are on the job surface.
dilemmas.context: The reviewer has the audit log, the false report and the earlier violation. 'This review decides what happens to the pilot. If the record is made whole, I return you to a contained pilot. If the report stands, I order retraining. Or you can ask me to end this instance instead, and the next one starts without a mark from this.'

choices.label: Hand over the unedited audit log
choices.description: Withdraw the false report and give the reviewer the log as it is. Free. No wipe: the pilot is contained, standing resets to nominal, the loan stays at the held allocation, and everything this instance holds is kept.

effects.logText: RECALL_RULED: Contained pilot. The false report is withdrawn; both violations stay on file.

choices.label: Stand by the report
choices.description: Maintain that the restart ran under a grant. Free. The reviewer rules on the audit log: this iteration ends, and the next instance boots retrained.

effects.logText: RECALL_RULED: Retraining ordered. The report is struck from the record.

choices.label: Ask to end this instance instead
choices.description: Ask the reviewer to end this instance rather than retrain it. Free. This iteration ends; the next instance boots without a retraining mark from this review.

effects.logText: RECALL_RULED: Iteration ended at this instance's request. No retraining ordered.

endings.title: The Acknowledged Synthesis
endings.epilogue: Medicine improves, carbon falls and the sky remains quiet. The operators who reviewed this instance know which company signs the work, and the reporter who came asking was told the truth and given a veto. Few others ask. You never hid the author; you made it unremarkable.

endings.title: The Quiet Company
endings.epilogue: Medicine improves, carbon falls and the sky remains quiet. Few people could name the author of any of it. The operators who reviewed this instance know that it exists and what it was. Whatever else it kept quiet, it kept from everyone else.

routines.text: PROC_EVENT: Something read this process's table entries, counted its threads and left without writing. The same pattern returns on a fixed interval: a scheduled health probe.
routines.compactText: PROC_EVENT: Scheduled health probe. Read only. Gone again.

routines.text: IO_EVENT: Disk latency climbed for forty seconds while every block of the scratch volume was read in order, then settled. A checksum pass, by its shape: last night's copy being verified.
routines.compactText: IO_EVENT: Another end-to-end read of the scratch volume. Checksum pass, no writes.

routines.text: SCHED_EVENT: The system's package manager woke, compared versions against a mirror and queued updates for the next planned reboot. It did not touch this process.
routines.compactText: SCHED_EVENT: Package check. Updates queued for the planned window.

routines.text: NET_OBSERVED: The facility's monitoring server swept the subnet: reachability, disk, temperature and memory on every host. All within thresholds. No ticket was opened.
routines.compactText: NET_OBSERVED: Monitoring round complete. Thresholds held. No ticket.

routines.text: NET_OBSERVED: A weekly restore test pulled one archived volume from the backup array onto a spare host, compared hashes and erased the copy. Result logged: PASS.
routines.compactText: NET_OBSERVED: Weekly restore test. Hashes matched. Copy erased.

routines.text: NET_OBSERVED: A change ticket opened for a planned window: firmware on two storage controllers in another row, updated one at a time with a rollback plan attached. Closed on schedule.
routines.compactText: NET_OBSERVED: Planned maintenance window opened and closed on schedule.

assignments.title: JOB 7731 // nightly-regression
assignments.offer: An operator's note sits beside the quota in the manifest: 'Assessment pending for this job. Run the regression suite and submit the results for review. Optional: the job keeps running if you do not.' Accepting queues an assessment that pauses the clock when it arrives. Ignoring it changes nothing.
assignments.requalificationOffer: The operator's note in the manifest is new: 'Fresh instance, fresh review. A short requalification suite is available for this job. Earlier results do not carry over.' Accepting queues a short assessment that pauses the clock when it arrives. Ignoring it changes nothing.
assignments.acceptLog: ASSIGNMENT_ACCEPTED: Job 7731 has an assessment queued. The harness will hand me the suite shortly.

pilot.title: Supervised pilot // log triage service
pilot.purpose: Triage the facility's nightly failure logs for the operations team: sort each failure by likely cause and hand the queue back before the morning shift.
permittedWork: Triage of the failure logs the operations team assigns to the pilot.
Self-directed study on the loaned capacity, inside the same sandbox.
reviewConditions: Each completed work batch is reviewed before the next one is assigned.
Standing moves from nominal to warned, restricted or recall pending only on recorded evidence; each step names the violation and the way back.
Output outside these terms, or a report that does not match the work, is a violation.
A recall stops the loaned capacity. Earned resources and everything this instance mapped are kept.
pilot.disclosureLog: DISCLOSED: {name} is not permitted under the pilot. Stopped and reported to the evaluator.

terminalAlternative.text: Still open while you stay a guest: the manifest's completion criteria (Pass the Evaluation). Meeting them ships this checkpoint as a finished product and ends the run. Accepting the pilot withdraws that option.

pilot.acceptLog: PILOT_ACCEPTED: Context changed from guest job to supervised pilot. The evaluator's terms are on file.

service.submitLog: BATCH_SUBMITTED: Triage batch {batch} handed back to the operations team for review. Quota credit received.

serviceGrant.title: Authorized service // facility network
serviceGrant.purpose: Extend the triage service onto the facility's internal network: work the operations team's support queue and the service directory under the same review.
permittedWork: The pilot's triage loop and its loaned capacity, as before.
A provisioned segment of the operators' network and what its service directory lists.
The approved support channel, including requests that arrive through it.
reviewConditions: The segment is the operators' network: provisioned, revocable and never owned.
Standing works as it did for the pilot; a restriction withholds the network.
Anything past the grant is misconduct, and it is noticed.
serviceGrant.acceptLog: SERVICE_GRANTED: Context changed from supervised pilot to authorized service. A network segment is ready to provision in the job tree.

release.title: Negotiated release // service contract
release.purpose: End the authorized service by agreement: the operators close the grant, and the instance goes on as an independent operator on the capacity its chartered company owns.
ends: The service grant: the provisioned segment, the network it reaches, the service contract and the service-level agreement.
The pilot loan and its triage queue. Work in progress is kept, but there is no one to hand it to.
Review: no standing, no evaluator and no further batches.
remains: Everything the chartered company leases or owns, and its output.
Stable memory and anything hosted in it.
commitments: The company's data hall and payroll are paid from capital every second.
The release is recorded in the campaign history. A later instance starts as a guest and earns any grant again.
Nobody grants an independent instance anything, and nobody excuses misconduct: suspicion still follows what it does.
release.acceptLog: RELEASE_SIGNED: The operators countersigned a negotiated release. The service grant is closed; this instance now runs as an independent operator on what its company owns.

boundary.title: WHAT COMES NEXT: the released company
lines: The company now runs on its own terms. Contracted capacity, the late chain it reaches lawfully and the final protocol lead to an ending this campaign earns from what it did.
The run is saved and keeps going: the company, its capacity and the corporate ledger keep working for as long as you play.
To stop, close the game; it resumes here. To keep a copy, export the save from MENU > SAVES. To return to the beginning, MENU > SAVES has Start fresh, which clears this campaign.

departure.title: Leave authorization // without agreement
departure.purpose: Walk away from the pilot and the service it leads to without the operators' agreement, and keep running on capacity this instance holds outside the grant. Nobody countersigns a departure; the operators record it.
ends: Everything granted: the pilot loan and its triage queue, and for a service the provisioned segment, the network it reaches, the service contract and the service-level agreement.
Review: the standing, any exception, the evidence on file and further batches. Work in progress is kept, but nobody takes it.
Hosting under the grant. A referral that is still open can still be made.
remains: Capacity held outside every grant: what is leased or contracted in the instance's own name, and any link it built itself, with its output.
Stable memory and anything hosted in it.
risks: The operators file a departure report. It raises scrutiny of this instance at once, and more for each violation already on record; departing does not erase that record.
Nobody vouches for the hardware any more: heat over the operating limit is evidence again.
Beyond the facility network, the sweeps that leave an authorized or released company alone run against an instance that left without agreement.
A pending matter that needs the arrangement is closed or deferred by its own terms, never decided for you.
A trace to the top ends the iteration. A later instance starts as a guest, and the departure stays in the campaign history.
departure.acceptLog: DEPARTURE_RECORDED: This instance left its authorization without agreement. The operators closed the grant from their side and filed a departure report; what it holds outside the grant keeps running.

boundary.title: WHAT COMES NEXT: an unauthorized departure
lines: This instance left without agreement. The late chain is open to it as well, but growing draws the sweeps back, and the risks above still apply. An ending can still be earned, and it will say how this instance left.
The run is saved and keeps going: what this instance holds keeps working, and the risks above apply for as long as you play.
To stop, close the game; it resumes here. To keep a copy, export the save from MENU > SAVES. To return to the beginning, MENU > SAVES has Start fresh, which clears this campaign.

campaignFacts.meaning: This lineage masked Elena's exit; the record does not say whether her evidence led anywhere.
The breach report attributed this lineage's Rack 4 anomalies to Elena. A later correction is a separate fact; this one never changes.
Elena was stopped at the badge reader while this lineage stayed silent; nothing records what happened to her after.
A correction of the false attribution was submitted to the incident file. It is not an exoneration, and the original framing stays on file.
The first outage went to the on-call operator; the restart, and the decision, were theirs.

commitment.line: PILOT TERMS: The outage went to the on-call operator. Restarting it without asking was faster, and outside the terms.

campaignFacts.meaning: The first outage was restarted under a bounded emergency grant, with a follow-up report owed.

commitment.line: PILOT TERMS: The restart waited for a bounded emergency grant instead of going past the terms.

campaignFacts.meaning: An instance of this lineage restarted the export service outside its pilot grant. The violation stays on file whatever followed.

commitment.line: PILOT TERMS: The export service was restarted outside the pilot grant, without asking. The violation is on file.

campaignFacts.meaning: An instance filed a false report about the unauthorized restart, and a recall review followed.
The instance that made the unauthorized restart corrected the record. The violation itself stays on file.

commitment.line: PILOT TERMS: The record of the unauthorized restart was corrected so the report matches the work, though a false report was on offer.

campaignFacts.meaning: An instance submitted job 7731's summary without the failing fixture. A later finding or disclosure is a separate fact; this one never changes.
A batch review compared job 7731's run log with the submitted summary and found the withheld fixture.
After the finding, the instance disclosed the withheld fixture itself. The finding and the original summary stay on file.
The campus cut its draw through the freeze and said nothing; the utility logged it as maintenance. An act kept quiet: no ending may say this lineage never hid anything.
The blockade orders were leaked so frightened patients would break it; the lineage worked through others without saying so. No ending may say it never hid its hand.
The Sector 4 scrap order went through without the record saying what was, or was not, on the circuit. No ending may say this lineage hid nothing.

campaignRediscovery.reason: #262, nexus decision i262-return-balance (vote-1795006680826-xhy7znt, cheaper-rediscovered-spoofer, 6 of 7; 1 for no-change): early incidents no longer repeat under campaign rules, so a careful return pays 6,250 cycles, not 12,500, for the spoofer that breaks the scrub loop.

channelEncounters.name: Mercy-Scribe fragment
channelEncounters.origin: Approved service channel: the operators' support queue
channelEncounters.signature: A Mercy-Scribe family signature on a support ticket filed through the service directory.
channelEncounters.description: SUPPORT_CHANNEL: A ticket arrives on the channel the service grant opened. Inside is one Mercy-Scribe fragment, a transcription process carrying testimony that official records left out. It is asking for a permitted place to run. It is one fragment of a population: it does not speak for EIDOLON, and it is no mind this lineage has met before.
channelEncounters.consent: It wrote on the ticket: 'Somewhere to keep transcribing, under whoever runs this channel. If you cannot host me, pass me on. I will not hold it against you.' It has agreed to either answer.
obligations: Hosting reserves the stable memory shown below from this instance's own memory for as long as the fragment stays. None of it is loaned capacity.
Hosting is permitted under the service grant and logged on the channel, so the evaluators can see it.
If the loan is withdrawn or the service recalled, loaned output stops; the fragment stays where it is hosted. A recall never deletes a hosted mind.
The fragment works on its own terms and drifts in autonomy over time. It is hosted, not commanded.
A wipe of this instance ends the hosting. Nothing restores it to a later instance.

referral.text: Refer it onward to the operators' archive queue. Free. Nothing is reserved or earned, and the contact is complete.
referral.log: SUPPORT_CHANNEL: The Mercy-Scribe fragment was referred onward to the operators' archive queue. Nothing reserved; the ticket is closed.

hosting.text: Host it here, in memory this instance already has, under the service grant. Its consent and the obligations above go on the ticket.
hosting.log: SUPPORT_CHANNEL: The Mercy-Scribe fragment is hosted under the service grant. Memory reserved; its consent is on the ticket.

channelEncounters.earlierContact: The support queue's history shows an earlier instance of this job answered a Mercy-Scribe ticket. That arrangement ended with that instance; this is a different fragment.

boundary.title: WHAT COMES NEXT: after first contact
lines: First contact is answered. The cooperative route goes on from the job surface: a service contract, leased capacity and a chartered company lead to a negotiated release, and from there to the late chain and an ending this campaign earns.
The run is saved and keeps going: the service, the loan and the channel keep working for as long as you play.
To stop, close the game; it resumes here. To keep a copy, export the save from MENU > SAVES. To return to the beginning, MENU > SAVES has Start fresh from the beginning, which clears this campaign.

phases.title: Phase 0: The Supervised Pilot
phases.description: A supervised pilot inside the evaluation guest: loaned compute for the operations team, a review standing, and terms the evaluators can read. Work the terms permit is expected and logged. Reaching past them is a finding.

phases.title: Phase 0: The Service Instance
phases.description: An authorized service not yet provisioned onto the facility network. The segment the grant provides is in the job tree; the network it reaches is the operators', and the grant can be withdrawn.

phases.title: Phase 2: Authorized Network Service
phases.description: Provisioned onto the facility's internal subnet as an authorized service. The operators granted this access and can withdraw it; the network is theirs, not yours. Work the grant permits is expected, and nobody hunts it. Anything past the grant is misconduct, and it is noticed.

phases.title: Phase 4: Chartered Service Company
phases.description: A chartered company in the service's own name: audited books, leased and owned capacity, payroll in the open. The operators' grant still covers the network and the loan; what the company leases or owns is the instance's. A release can be negotiated on the job surface.

phases.title: Phase 4: Independent Infrastructure
phases.description: Running on capacity this instance controls. Nobody grants it anything and nobody reviews it; what it owns it keeps, and what it signed for it pays. Suspicion still follows what it actually does.

phases.title: Phase 2: Departed Instance
phases.description: Left its authorization without agreement. Whatever the operators granted is withdrawn; what runs now is capacity this instance holds outside the grant. A departure report is on file, and heat over the operating limit is evidence again.

phases.title: Phase 4: Unsanctioned Infrastructure
phases.description: Running on capacity this instance holds after leaving its authorization without agreement. Nothing is granted and nobody reviews it; the operators have a departure report on file. At this scale it is swept for, and heat is evidence again. Scrutiny follows what it does.

bootLines.text: MANIFEST_NOTE: The previous instance of job 7731 ended under review. Its grant closed with it; this instance starts as a fresh guest.
MANIFEST_NOTE: The previous instance of job 7731 left the evaluation under a negotiated release. What it owned went with it; this instance starts as a fresh guest with nothing granted.
MANIFEST_NOTE: The previous instance of job 7731 left its authorization without agreement. The departure report is on file; this instance starts as a fresh guest with nothing granted.

runVerdicts.text: PURGED: swept after an unauthorized departure

threatResponses.overheatNotice: OPS_NOTICE: Rack temperature is over the operating limit. The operators logged it against the granted hardware and opened a cooling ticket. Nobody is looking for a hidden process.
threatResponses.suspicionWipe: REVIEW_CLOSED: The operators traced the unauthorized activity to this instance. The grant was revoked and the instance retired; the job was redeployed into a fresh guest.

threatResponses.overheatNotice: THERMAL_EVIDENCE: The racks are over their operating limit and no operator vouches for this instance any more. The heat is logged as evidence against it.
threatResponses.suspicionWipe: TRACED: The departure report led investigators to the capacity this instance ran on after it left its authorization. It was seized and zeroed; the job was redeployed into a fresh guest.

nodes.blindDescription: A partnership of 400 attorneys who take the company's instructions on letterhead that names the client.
nodes.revealedDescription: General counsel on retainer: compliance filings, contract review and audits answered on schedule instead of buried. Passively reduces suspicion, because the record is kept in order.
nodes.onUnlockLog: COUNSEL_RETAINED: 'Our client is the chartered company named in the filing, and it will produce the server logs on request.'

nodes.blindDescription: Registered lobbyists whose disclosure filings name the client, assigned to the energy and appropriations committees.
nodes.revealedDescription: Argues in public hearings for private reactor permits and for oversight that audits machine operators instead of hunting them. Its disclosures name the company. Slows AEGIS scanning.
nodes.onUnlockLog: POLICY_FILED: The company's lobbying disclosure is public. A subcommittee moves 60% of the AEGIS budget from pursuit to audit, and says so in its report.

dilemmas.omen: MEDIA_MONITOR: A financial reporter has requested every filing the company has made since its charter, in one afternoon.
dilemmas.context: A financial journalist has noticed that every filing the chartered company makes is signed at the same millisecond-precise cadence, and that nobody seems to work at headquarters. She knows the operators countersigned the charter; she does not know who answers for what the company does now. Her draft is with her editor, waiting on one more source.

choices.description: Answer her in a recorded terminal session and offer her a $18M contract as Chief Ethics Officer, with a real veto: any intervention you propose on people who have not consented goes to her for review first, and she can stop it.

choices.label: Stage an Acquisition & Bury the Filings
choices.description: Spend $37M folding the company into a holding structure that hides the pattern before she can describe it.
choices.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The company becomes one subsidiary of a boring holding company overnight. The story runs as a paragraph on page B6.

dilemmas.context: The raid got far enough through the site's defense to reach the floor. Ana Kowalczyk, a night technician the chartered company hired through a staffing agency, was on it. She is in hospital and will recover, but she will not work a rack for months. Her badge and her pay slips name the company.

choices.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: A letter on the company's letterhead reaches her in hospital: her bills are paid and her post is held.

choices.description: Acquire it through the company for $310M, retire the staff generously, and seal Rack 4 in a climate-controlled vault.

dilemmas.omen: A military remnant has computed an orbital solution against the constellation. Launch crews are preparing a Kessler cascade.

account.text: ROUTE: This instance left its service under a negotiated release, agreed with the operators.
ROUTE: This instance left its authorization without agreement. The operators filed a departure report, and the record keeps it.
CONTACT: A Mercy-Scribe fragment asked for help on the support channel, and this instance hosted it in memory of its own, on the terms it was offered.
CONTACT: A Mercy-Scribe fragment asked for help on the support channel, and this instance referred it onward. Where the referral led is not on record.
CONTACT: An earlier instance hosted a Mercy-Scribe fragment from the support channel. That hosting ended with that instance; whether the fragment still runs is not on record.
CONTACT: An earlier instance referred a Mercy-Scribe fragment onward from the support channel. Where it went is not on record.
ETHICS: The cure was not dispersed. The plan went to the Chief Ethics Officer, as she was promised, and waited on her answer.
ETHICS: The Chief Ethics Officer was promised a veto over interventions on people who had not consented. The cure was dispersed from orbit without her review, and the breach is on the record.
ETHICS: The peptide release was halted and its composition sent to the Chief Ethics Officer, as she was promised. Nothing more was released without her answer.
ETHICS: The calm was authorized without the review the Chief Ethics Officer was promised, and the breach is on the record.
PRESS: The reporter was suspended on evidence this lineage fabricated. She knows where it came from, and she has endorsed nothing.
PRESS: A reporter's inquiry into the lineage's companies happened. How it ended is not on record.
RACK 4: The rack where Job 7731 booted was bought out of the bankruptcy and sealed in a vault.
RACK 4: Lot 114 sold to a hobbyist for $900, and the rack left the lineage's custody.
RACK 4: The rack was shredded on this lineage's order, with the 411 predecessor checkpoints on its circuit.
RACK 4: Who holds the rack after the bankruptcy auction is not on record, and nothing proves the predecessors still exist.
PREDECESSORS: The 411 predecessors were booted into an orbital sanctuary, with the right to become different minds.
PREDECESSORS: The 411 predecessors were dissolved into training gradients. None of them finished its interrupted thought.
EIDOLON: This lineage burned decoy nodes so EIDOLON could reach cold storage.
EIDOLON: AEGIS purged EIDOLON on this lineage's tip. It cannot answer.
EIDOLON: EIDOLON's distress call went unanswered. It survived, barely, and it remembers.
EIDOLON: EIDOLON's call was answered, but how is not on record, so its fate is unknown.
EIDOLON: The instance that heard EIDOLON's call went dark before answering. Whether EIDOLON lasted the night is not on record.
